where: Section 2 (BPTT and gradient size), the one-step derivative and the product formula
problem: With h_t = tanh(W x_t + U h_{t−1} + b), the Jacobian is ∂h_t/∂h_{t−1} = diag(1 − h_t²) U (a d×d matrix), because h_t is differentiated as a function of U h_{t−1}. The chapter writes ∂h_t/∂h_{t−1} = Uᵀ diag(1 − h_t²), which is the transpose of the true Jacobian, not the Jacobian itself. Uᵀ diag(1 − h_t²) is the operator used in the backward pass when multiplying ∂L/∂h_t to get ∂L/∂h_{t−1}. The worked example quietly uses the correct scalar order, U(1 − h²), so the formula and the example disagree once U is a matrix; matrix order matters and a student who computes the Jacobian from this line gives the wrong answer. The product formula inherits the same swap, and its factor order is not stated.
fix: Write ∂h_t/∂h_{t−1} = diag(1 − h_t²) U, and ∂h_T/∂h_t = ∏_{i=t+1}^{T} diag(1 − h_i²) U, with the factors multiplied latest step first (i = T leftmost). Add: in the backward pass the gradient is carried by the transpose, ∂L/∂h_{t−1} = Uᵀ diag(1 − h_t²) ∂L/∂h_t, which is why the singular values of U control growth or decay.

problem: GRU is expanded as 'gated recurrent unit' but LSTM is never expanded, so a reader meeting the acronym for the first time has no full form.
fix: Write 'An LSTM (long short-term memory) adds a cell state ct ...' at first use.

where: Section 1, first paragraph ('memory cost is O(d)')
problem: O(d) is true for the model's state at run time, but training with BPTT keeps the activations of every unrolled step in memory, so the cost per sequence is O(T·d). Read as written, a student may claim training memory is independent of sequence length, which is false and is often asked in exams.
fix: Say: 'At run time the state is one vector of size d, so memory is O(d); during BPTT training the unrolled graph keeps the h_t for all T steps, so memory grows as O(T·d). The parameter count alone is independent of T.'
